items.title: ScienceDaily: Breathing less oxygen tripled lifespan in mice with a deadly brain disorder
items.content_text: Oxygen is essential for life, but too much of it can become dangerously toxic, particularly in people with certain neurological and mitochondrial disorders. Scientists at Gladstone Institutes have discovered that defective proteins can disrupt the ability of mitochondria to consume oxygen, allowing harmful levels to accumulate in tissues. Remarkably, mice with a genetic disorder that causes motor neuron degeneration lived three times longer when they breathed air containing less oxygen.
